method: Per task, best first: public leaderboards with open-weights views (Artificial Analysis, arena.ai, OpenArt) as of Sep/Oct 2026, then official claims, then community comparisons. Figures read through a summarising fetch; spot-check before quoting exact numbers. Where no board covers a pair of families the order is marked as inference in `why`.

compose-multi-image.gloss: combine several images (put X into scene Y, outfit onto person)

control.gloss: image guided by edges/depth/pose of another image

control-map.gloss: make the edges/depth map a control input needs, from a raw photo or clip; keep a video's motion and layout while restyling it (watercolor, anime, clay, painting style)

edit-identity.gloss: keep a person/character/product while changing the rest

flf2v.gloss: video between a first and a last frame: morph or transition from one image to the next, keyframes

frame-from-video.gloss: one frame of a clip as an image (to restyle or edit it, then start a video from it)

i2v.gloss: video starting from an image, animate a photo

inpaint.gloss: repaint a masked part of an image

join-clips.gloss: several clips played as one continuous video: stitch, merge, concatenate segments in order

motion-transfer.gloss: make a still character move or dance like the person in a video

multi-angle.gloss: the same subject or character from other camera angles: views, turnaround, angle sheet, front side back

outpaint.gloss: extend an image beyond its borders

person-from-reference.gloss: a real person from their photo in new images or videos: an influencer, a model, the same person in a new scene, pose, outfit or angle, photoreal, consistent across shots

product-on-model.gloss: a given person wearing or holding a given product (jacket, shirt, watch, headphones, bag): product ad, ad shot, lookbook, try-on, model with product, at an exact size or aspect ratio

reference-video.gloss: video of a subject/product/sheet read as a reference (not as a frame)

stack-clips.gloss: several clips side by side in one frame: split screen, montage, grid, stacked videos

t2i-text.gloss: image with legible text (posters, signs, packaging)

talking-head.gloss: a person speaking, talking, saying a line or singing to camera (lip-sync, voice, dialogue)

upscale-image.gloss: enlarge, sharpen or restore an image: higher resolution, 2K, 4K, 8K

upscale-video.gloss: enlarge, sharpen, restore or clean up a video: higher resolution, 1080p, 4K, old or grainy footage

video-character-replace.gloss: replace or swap the person/dancer in an existing video with a character, keep the moves and background

video-object-replace.gloss: change, swap or replace one object inside an existing clip or video, leave the rest as it is

product-on-model.recipe_hint: route: Z-Image Turbo scene -> FLUX.2 klein 2-reference edits
product-on-model.why: the only way here to get an EXACT size with the person's identity AND the exact product: render the ad scene at the delivery size, then edit the person and the product into it (a reference edit keeps its first image's shape). Each stage is an official template; the chain is assembled from them.

route.does: the ad scene at the exact delivery width/height: setting, light, framing, and a stand-in model in the same pose wearing a plain item of the product's kind (a jacket, a watch, headphones)
reference_image_1 = the scene (sets the shape), reference_image_2 = the person's photo: the person from image 2 takes the stand-in's place, same pose, framing and light
reference_image_1 = that result, reference_image_2 = the product photo: the person in image 1 wears or holds the exact product from image 2 (colour, print, logo, hardware)
the exact delivery width x height (the edits keep the scene's shape at about 1 MP)

constraints: three stages; set the scene's width/height to the delivery size

product-on-model.why: one stage, the official template's own default (a woman + a handbag: 'Let this character hold the bag with both hands'); the result has the PERSON PHOTO's shape, so it fits only when that is the shape wanted
constraints: size follows the person photo (aspect ratio), about 1 MP

product-on-model.why: one stage multi-image edit (image 1 = the person, image 2 = the product); output follows image 1
the only official open template that takes a person + a garment AND an exact width/height ('Replace costumes for the character'); its note warns sizes far from image 1's can shift the edit

inpaint.why: official inpainting template on Qwen-Image; repaints the masked area from the prompt
constraints: the mask is the image's transparent area (painted in ComfyUI's mask editor, or a PNG with alpha)
repaints from TEXT: it cannot copy a specific product from a reference photo
repaints from text, not from a reference

inpaint.why: light and fast; lower quality than the two above

outpaint.why: official FLUX.1 Fill outpaint template: pad the sides, fill them from the prompt

person-from-reference.recipe_hint: route: Qwen Image 2.1 still at the delivery size, with the body read off their photo -> Qwen Image 2.1 BFS head swap with their photo
person-from-reference.why: ANY job that recreates a real person from their photoreal photo: a still, angles, an ad, a video. The body is read off the photo (ethnicity, skin, body size, bust, belly, age, hair), so the shot is free and the body stays theirs; the head swap puts their own face on it, keeping the shot's gaze and expression. Both render at 1024x1536, fixed (smaller or larger, the face came out long and narrow; a video model resizes its first frame by itself) — no upscale and no realism pass after them: a Z-Image pass changed her face and made the skin plastic, an upscaler added nothing a native render lacks. Every later step reads the swapped still. Tested on Comfy Cloud 2026-10-07: the only route here that kept her face and figure; edits of her photo (Qwen 2511, FLUX.2 klein) changed her face or body.

evidence.src: Comfy Cloud test, red-jacket influencer case, 2026-10-07

constraints: photoreal people only (illustration and anime keep their own routes)
a clear face photo; with several, the one closest to the shot's head angle

route.does: the shot (outfit, pose, framing, setting, light, gaze, expression) with the person's body as their photo shows it; their photo is read, not rendered from
target = that still, face = their photo: their face and hair on it, everything else kept
